newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf Arab states to meet on Iran, Mideast peace.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Arab states to meet on Iran, Mideast peace.

text.p: Gulf Arab foreign ministers will meet in Riyadh on Saturday to assess the election of moderate Mohammad Khatami as Iran's next president, the United Arab Emirates news agency WAM said on Tuesday.
Talks by the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) officials will also focus on the stalled Middle East peace process and Turkey's two-week incursion into northern Iraq, it said.

Ministers from Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, the UAE and Bahrain had been scheduled to hold regular consultations in Riyadh on June 7. Gulf officials were not available for comment on why the talks were brought forward.
"Authoritative sources told WAM the council would discuss ties between the GCC and Tehran in light of recent election results," the agency said.

GCC leaders, who view their neighbour Iran with suspicion, have congratulated Khatami on his landslide victory. But diplomats said most would adopt a wait-and-see approach towards Tehran before deciding on how to move next.

Iran is trying to improve ties with its Gulf Arab neighbours, which have accused Tehran of interfering in their internal affairs -- a charge Iran denies -- and voiced concern over its armament programme.
The sources told WAM the council would also discuss Iran's "continued occupation" of the three islands of the Greater and Lesser Tunbs and Abu Musa, which are also claimed by the UAE.
Khatami on Tuesday told his first news conference since his election that the islands belonged to Iran but urged bilateral talks to settle the territorial dispute.
Khatami, a former culture minister was elected on Saturday. He will take over in August from President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani.
Though most GCC states remain enemies of Iraqi President Saddam Hussein since his 1990 invasion of Kuwait, their media have criticised Turkey's cross-border offensive against Kurdish rebels.
